lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: two-variable relationships and their graphs

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A tank holds 100 litres and is filling at 9 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 289 litres?
A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.
Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.
The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $115 call-out fee plus $11 per hour. A job cost $148 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = 2bh + 3 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $5 each and item B costs $3 each. You may spend at most $220 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 30 litres and is filling at 16 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 318 litres?
A model gives a required side length of −6 metres. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Add 6 to every measurement to correct the model.
Reject the solution; a length cannot be negative, so it lies outside the model’s domain.
Use 6 metres, taking the absolute value.
Report −6 metres, because the algebra is correct.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $300 call-out fee plus $21 per hour. A job cost $636 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: The formula A = -5bh − 2 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $15 each and item B costs $15 each. You may spend at most $210 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 115 litres and is filling at 12 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 223 litres?
A budget model allows 12.7 units of a product sold individually. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Split the order so the fractional unit is shared.
Round down to 12; buying a partial unit is not possible and 13 would exceed the budget.
Report 12.7, because the constraint is satisfied.
Round up to 13, because 12.7 is closer to 13.
